title: GodLike and Orangutan Give India Two Teams in PUBG Mobile World Cup Grand Finals for the First Time
excerpt: Orangutan qualified directly from Group A with 91 points and two Chicken Dinners, while GodLike advanced from Group B as India doubled its presence at the $3 million Paris event.
body:
• India has two teams in the PUBG Mobile World Cup Grand Finals for the first time — GodLike Esports and Orangutan both advanced through the Group Stage in Paris.
  • Orangutan finished second in Group A with 91 points and two Chicken Dinners across 12 matches, qualifying directly for the Grand Finals.
  • GodLike Esports, the reigning BMPS 2026 champions, advanced from Group B to keep India's double representation alive.
  • The Grand Finals run from August 14 to 16 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, with $1.7 million in prize money on the line and the Smash Rule deciding the champion.

Orangutan's Strong Group Stage Run

Orangutan locked in their Grand Finals spot after a commanding Group A performance at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. The Indian squad finished second out of 16 teams with 91 points — 41 from placements and 50 from eliminations — across 12 matches played on August 6 and 7, according to results tracked by EsportsVerse.

https://x.com/DDIndialive/status/2086777080482787440

The team picked up two Chicken Dinners during the Group Stage, including a dominant 20-point match and a 21-point match on day two. Pakistan's 4Thrives Esports topped Group A with 107 points, followed by Orangutan, Aurora Gaming from Mongolia at 90 points, Team Flash from Vietnam at 89, and Nigma Galaxy at 88 to complete the five direct qualifiers.

Orangutan earned their spot in the World Cup by topping the Krafton India Esports points table. This is their second international appearance after representing India at PMGC 2025, where they marked India's return to PUBG Mobile's top global event after a three-year absence.

GodLike's Path Through Group B

GodLike Esports, who entered as BMPS 2026 champions after winning the finals in Jaipur in June, competed in Group B on August 8 and 9. The group was widely considered the tougher draw, featuring defending PMWC champions Yangon Galacticos from Myanmar, Alpha7 Esports from Brazil, and NongShim RedForce from South Korea.

GodLike's qualification extends a remarkable 2026 run for the organization. After a shaky start to the domestic season that saw them relegated to Group B in BMPS Round 2, the team rallied behind Spower and Admino to top both Group B and Group A in subsequent rounds before winning the Grand Finals in Jaipur, according to SportsAdda's coverage of the Indian qualifying scene.

"India has never had more than one team here before."

— SportsAdda

A Historic Milestone for Indian Esports

Having two Indian teams at a PUBG Mobile World Cup is unprecedented. Last year in Riyadh, India had just one representative — AxTMG — in a 24-team field. The 2026 tournament expanded to 32 teams, and India now holds two of those slots.

The broader Esports World Cup 2026, which the PUBG Mobile tournament sits within, is being held in Paris after organizers moved the entire event from Riyadh on May 20. The overall EWC features 25 game tournaments with a combined $75 million prize pool. Indian organizations GodLike and S8UL also compete in other EWC titles including Chess and Free Fire.

What's at Stake in the Grand Finals

The Grand Finals run from August 14 to 16, featuring 16 teams competing in up to 18 matches. Ten of those teams qualified directly from the Group Stage — five from each group — while six more will come through the Survival Stage on August 11 and 12.

The Grand Finals carry $1.7 million in prize money, with the champion taking home $650,000. Day three uses the Smash Rule: a points threshold is set after match 12, and the first team to win a match after crossing that threshold claims the title outright.

For Indian viewers, the timing is unusually favorable. Matches start at 4:30 PM IST, with dedicated South Asia and India broadcasts running alongside the English stream. The tournament streams free on the official Esports World Cup YouTube and Twitch channels.
